name: Orange County Museum of Art
overview: Art museum at the Segerstrom Center for the Arts, 3333 Avenue of the Arts, Costa Mesa. Since 29 September 2025 the UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art, run by the University of California, Irvine (UC Irvine).

Founded in 1962 as the Fine Arts Patrons Pavilion Gallery at the Balboa Pavilion by 13 women. By 1968 it was the Newport Harbor Art Museum, it opened a 23,000 square foot building in Newport Beach in 1977, and it took the name Orange County Museum of Art after a merger completed in July 1996 with Laguna Art Museum (Wikipedia).
Building: designed by Morphosis, 53,000 square feet, cost $98 million (UC Irvine). Ground was broken in September 2019 and it opened on 8 October 2022 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Orange County Museum of Art: private donors until 2025: the Segerstrom family and other trustees; now a unit of the public University of California, Irvine
wider_context: Mordechai "Moti" Ferder, the Lugano Diamonds head named by Hyperallergic as the donor of the $2.5 million free-admission gift, was accused of fraud, civil theft and other financial crimes in several lawsuits, and resigned as CEO of Lugano Diamonds and Jewelry in May 2025 (Matt Stromberg, Hyperallergic, 1 October 2025).
Hyperallergic reports that Ferder's 2022 donation established free admission at OCMA for 10 years, and an OCMA representative said in 2025 that the pledge is current.

press_items.title: Matt Stromberg, "UC Irvine Takes Over Orange County Museum of Art" (1 October 2025)

name: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke
overview: Duke University's art museum, at 2001 Campus Drive on Duke's central campus in Durham, North Carolina.

Founded in 1969 as the Duke University Museum of Art in a former science building on East Campus, starting with 200 medieval works from the Ernest Brummer Collection (museum website). The new building opened on 2 October 2005 (INDY Week; the museum website gives 2005).
Named for Raymond D. Nasher, a Duke alumnus, Texas real estate developer and sculpture collector, who gave $7.5 million in 1998 for a new museum and died on 16 March 2007 (museum website).
funding_verdict: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke: mainly university-funded: Duke University allocation, endowment income and gifts from private donors and foundations
wider_context: History of the Duke Endowment: James B. Duke created it on 11 December 1924 with $40 million, invested primarily in Duke Power Company stock. Duke founded the American Tobacco Company in 1890 and is described as a tobacco and electric power industrialist (Wikipedia).
The Endowment funds acquisitions and exhibitions at the museum, which is the connection.

name: Museum of Arts and Design
overview: Museum of contemporary craft, art and design at 2 Columbus Circle, New York (museum website).

Opened in 1956 as the Museum of Contemporary Crafts, with the philanthropist Aileen Osborn Webb a key force behind it. It became the American Craft Museum in 1979 and took the name Museum of Arts and Design in 2002 (Wikipedia).

In 2002 it won a bid to buy the building at 2 Columbus Circle. The architect Brad Cloepfil of Allied Works Architecture redesigned it as the Jerome and Simona Chazen Building with a glazed terra-cotta facade, giving more than 54,000 square feet, over three times the former space. Changes to the Edward Durell Stone building sparked a preservation debate (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Museum of Arts and Design: private nonprofit: donors, with New York State and City arts agencies

press_items.title: Benjamin Sutton, report on the lawsuit by the former chief financial officer (26 March 2024)

name: Palm Springs Art Museum
overview: Art museum at 101 Museum Drive, Palm Springs, with 28 galleries, two sculpture gardens, an 85-seat lecture hall and a 433-seat theater (museum website).

Founded in 1938 as the Palm Springs Desert Museum at La Plaza in downtown Palm Springs. It built its first permanent structure in 1958 and changed its name to Palm Springs Art Museum in April 2005 (museum website). Wikipedia gives the renaming year as 1982.

The board named Christine Vendredi executive director on 29 September 2025. She had been interim director since April and joined as chief curator in April 2024 (Palm Springs Post, 29 September 2025). Adam Lerner, director since summer 2021, resigned in the spring (Los Angeles Times, Christopher Knight, 10 November 2025). The board chair is Craig Hartzman (museum website).
funding_verdict: Palm Springs Art Museum: mixed: donations, endowment draws and earned income

Christopher Knight, "Commentary: Audit questions roil the Palm Springs Art Museum" (18 November 2025)
Helen, "Whistleblower Complaint Alleges Misconduct at Palm Springs Art Museum" (29 April 2026)

name: Portland Museum of Art
overview: Art museum at 7 Congress Square in Portland, Maine, with a public car park at 120 Free Street (museum site).
Founded in 1882 as the Portland Society of Art. Wikipedia calls it the largest and oldest public art institution in Maine.
The Charles Shipman Payson Building, designed by Henry Nichols Cobb of I. M. Pei & Partners, opened in 1983 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Portland Museum of Art: contribution-led: foundations and corporate sponsors, with a Maine Arts Commission grant
wider_context: TD Bank N.A. pleaded guilty on 10 October 2024 to conspiring to fail to maintain an anti-money laundering programme, fail to file accurate currency transaction reports and launder monetary instruments, in a combined $1.8 billion resolution (US Department of Justice).

The museum's Art for All page lists the TD Charitable Foundation among its corporate sponsors. A 21 October 2009 article on vermontbiz.com, "TD Bank supports area organizations with $29,000 through charitable foundation", says the foundation is the charitable giving arm of TD Bank N.A.

press_items.title: Alison Frazee, Director of Advocacy, "The Column Advocacy News" (17 April 2025, advocacy source)
Megan Gray, "Dispute over Portland Museum of Art expansion now in judge's hands" (5 March 2025, local press)

name: Georgia O'Keeffe Museum
overview: Private non-profit museum devoted to Georgia O'Keeffe, with galleries at 217 Johnston Street in Santa Fe, a Welcome Center in Abiquiú and two historic O'Keeffe homes in northern New Mexico (museum website; Albuquerque Journal).
Founded in November 1995 by Anne Windfohr Marion and John L. Marion, part-time Santa Fe residents. Opened on 17 July 1997 (Wikipedia).
The main building was designed by Richard Gluckman with Allegretti Architects (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Georgia O'Keeffe Museum: private philanthropy and earned income: a family foundation started it; admissions, retail and an endowment sustain it

name: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture
overview: Nine-week summer residency programme for emerging artists on a campus at 39 Art School Road, Madison, Maine, where participants live and work together with resident and visiting faculty artists. The Maine campus is generally not open to the public (Skowhegan).
Founded in 1946 by the artists Willard "Bill" Cummings, Sidney Simon, Henry Varnum Poor and Charles Cutler, on the Cummings family farm (Skowhegan).
Building and site: a former farm. The campus was extended under the 75th anniversary campaign with a sculpture shop, ceramics studio, dining hall, studios and staff cottages (Morning Sentinel, 2023).
funding_verdict: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture: privately funded: foundations, alumni and individual donors, an annual awards dinner and an endowment

name: SECCA
overview: Contemporary art museum formerly SECCA, now called the North Carolina Museum of Art, Winston-Salem (NCMA Winston-Salem). The Marguerite Drive campus (750 Marguerite Dr.) is closed in 2026 for construction improvements. A free downtown exhibition and program space at 400 W. Fourth St., Suite 130, was announced on 21 May 2026 to open on 16 July and is open Wednesday through Sunday (NCMA Winston-Salem).

Founded in 1956 by Winston-Salem professionals and artists who wanted their city to be a place for Southeastern artists to show their work, first as the Gallery of Fine Art on Trade Street. It moved to Old Salem in the 1960s and later became the Winston-Salem Gallery of Contemporary Art (WFDD).
In 1972 the industrialist James G. Hanes willed his 32-acre estate to the gallery (NCMA Winston-Salem history page).
funding_verdict: SECCA: mainly public: a North Carolina state agency, with private donors for the downtown space and programmes

name: Odesa National Fine Arts Museum
overview: Art museum in the Potocki Palace at 5-a Sofiivska Street in central Odesa.

Opened in November 1899 through the efforts of the Odesa Society of Fine Arts; mayor Hryhoriy Marazli bought the palace in 1888 and transferred it to the city in 1892 for the museum (museum's About page).
English Wikipedia says Seweryn Potocki ordered the palace and building began in 1805; the museum dates the palace to the 1820s.
funding_verdict: Odesa National Fine Arts Museum: mainly public: the Ukrainian state, with foreign heritage funds for war repairs
wider_context: A Russian missile strike on the night of 5 to 6 November 2023 damaged the building and seven exhibitions; a strike on 20 July 2023 had already damaged it (Ukrainian Wikipedia).
Russia neither funds nor controls the museum, so the attacks are context for the repair money, not a mark against the museum.

name: Fundación Ama Amoedo
overview: Foundation supporting contemporary Latin American art, based at Casa Neptuna, a residency house by the ocean and surrounded by native forest in José Ignacio, Uruguay (Fundación Ama Amoedo).

Founder and president Amalia Amoedo is a philanthropist, patron and art collector who has supported artists and cultural institutions for more than twenty years. The foundation runs through a non-profit established in Uruguay in 2021 for programmes, residencies and initiatives with regional and international reach, and one established in Argentina in 2025 to channel support to artists, cultural spaces, publications and projects there (Fundación Ama Amoedo).
Named for its founder. Verónica Flom is director (Fundación Ama Amoedo).
funding_verdict: Fundación Ama Amoedo: privately run by its founder; her family's Loma Negra cement fortune is background history

name: State Museum of Arts of the Republic of Karakalpakstan (Savitsky Museum)
overview: State art museum in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, holding close to 100,000 works from the mid-20th century on, including Russian avant-garde and local folk art (The Art Newspaper, 2025). Wikipedia gives more than 82,000 items.
Established in 1966 at the initiative of Igor Savitsky, its first curator (Wikipedia).

Named for Igor Savitsky (The Art Newspaper calls it the I.V. Savitsky State Art Museum). The Art Newspaper describes Savitsky as an "art-loving Soviet bureaucrat" who collected Modern art from Russia and Central Asia that was risky to collect in the Soviet Union.
funding_verdict: Savitsky Museum (Nukus): state museum; the government-backed Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF) pays for specialists, restoration, renovation and digitisation
wider_context: Hyperallergic (Nevdon Jamgochian, "The Bukhara Biennial Will Break Your Heart", 27 October 2025) calls the Bukhara Biennial, supported by the state-funded Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation, a case of artwashing and says its existence "depends on a restrictive autocratic structure". The piece does not name the Nukus museum.

The Spectator Australia (Alex Diggins, "Am I a useful idiot visiting Uzbekistan's first art biennial?", 3 January 2026) quotes an unnamed artist who said the biennial had "art-washy vibes"; the author travelled on a trip sponsored by ACDF, which the piece calls the show's organisers.

ACDF supports the Bukhara Biennial (Hyperallergic) and organises it (The Spectator Australia), and is the body that paid for the Savitsky Museum's specialists, restorers and renovation (The Art Newspaper, 2025).

press_items.title: George Nelson, "Uzbekistan's troubled Nukus Museum embroiled in new row" (2019)

name: State Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan
overview: National art museum in central Tashkent, at 16 Amir Temur Avenue (Wikipedia). Its collection numbers more than 100,000 works (Designboom).
Founded in 1918 as the Museum of People University, later renamed the Central Arts Museum. Named the Tashkent Art Museum in 1924 and the Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan in 1935 (Wikipedia).
Its first collection was a hundred works of art from Grand Duke Nicholas Konstantinovich of Russia and other private collections (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: State Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan: state: the new building is commissioned by the government-backed Art and Culture Development Foundation
wider_context: Hyperallergic (Nevdon Jamgochian, "The Bukhara Biennial Will Break Your Heart", 27 October 2025) calls the Bukhara Biennial, supported by the state-funded Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation, a case of artwashing and says its existence "depends on a restrictive autocratic structure". It says Amnesty International continues to report widespread censorship and harassment of journalists in Uzbekistan. The piece does not name the Tashkent museum.

The Spectator Australia (Alex Diggins, "Am I a useful idiot visiting Uzbekistan's first art biennial?", 3 January 2026) quotes an unnamed artist who said the biennial had "art-washy vibes" and felt "for the government, not the people". The author's trip was sponsored by ACDF, which the piece calls the show's organisers.
ACDF, which supports the Bukhara Biennial (Hyperallergic) and organises it (The Spectator Australia), is the body commissioning the new building (Designboom; ACDF website).

name: Vanuatu Cultural Centre (Vanuatu Kaljoral Senta)
overview: National cultural institution of Vanuatu in the capital, Port Vila. It describes itself as a statutory body whose role covers preserving, protecting and promoting Vanuatu's cultural heritage (centre's website).

Wikipedia gives its founding as 1955 and describes it as an umbrella organisation with the National Museum, a National Film and Sound Unit, the National Archives, the National Library and Public Library, a Fieldworkers' Unit, the Tafea Cultural Centre in Lenakel (Tanna) and the Malekula Cultural Centre.
The Oral Traditions Collection Project began in 1976 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Vanuatu Cultural Centre: Vanuatu government funds the curator's post; earthquake recovery aided by UNESCO's Heritage Emergency Fund

name: Fundación Oswaldo Vigas
overview: Non-profit foundation based in Caracas that works to deepen understanding of the Venezuelan painter Oswaldo Vigas and to keep a selection of his work preserved and accessible to institutions, curators, writers and art lovers (Fundación Oswaldo Vigas).

Named for Oswaldo Vigas, a Venezuelan painter, muralist and sculptor born in 1923 in Valencia, Carabobo, who died in Caracas on 22 April 2014. Wikipedia calls him the first artist to represent Venezuela at the Venice Biennale, in 1954.
Wikipedia states the foundation "was created to expand his art legacy worldwide."
funding_verdict: Fundación Oswaldo Vigas: artist-estate foundation chaired by Lorenzo Vigas

name: Fundación Sala Mendoza
overview: Independent, non-profit exhibition space run as a civil association that practises self-management (Fundación Sala Mendoza).
It states a continuous commitment to art creation and knowledge exchange since 1956 (Fundación Sala Mendoza).
Started by Luisa Rodríguez de Mendoza and Eugenio Mendoza (Fundación Sala Mendoza).
funding_verdict: Fundación Sala Mendoza: started by Luisa Rodríguez de Mendoza and Eugenio Mendoza; runs a bookstore and an Amigos de la Sala membership programme

name: Nguyen Art Foundation
overview: Non-profit contemporary art organisation in Ho Chi Minh City with two permanent sites inside EMASI schools: EMASI Nam Long (147 Street No. 8, Nam Long Residential Area, District 7) and EMASI Van Phuc (2 Street No. 5, Van Phuc Residential City, Thu Duc City) (Wikipedia).

Founded in 2018 by collector Quynh Nguyen, who describes it as "a branching support structure" for contemporary art in Vietnam with four strands: collection, exhibitions, education and public programmes, and development projects (NAF website).
It grew out of Nguyen's personal collection (Vietcetera, Valeria Mertsalova). Wikipedia puts the collection at more than 1,000 works, mainly by artists from Vietnam and Southeast Asia.
funding_verdict: Nguyen Art Foundation: self-funded: the Nguyen family's private money

name: National Gallery of Arts Tirana
overview: Albania's national art gallery on the "Martyrs of the Nation" Boulevard in central Tirana (Wikipedia). It closed for reconstruction in October 2021 (Wikipedia, whose infobox says until December 2023). Shqiptarja reported on 15 October 2025 that the work was still going on.

Traces its origin to a group of Albanian artists and the Arts Committee of 1946. The Gallery of Arts opened to the public on 11 January 1954 (Wikipedia). The article gives 29 November 1974 for the new venue's opening but its infobox gives 1956, so the dates conflict.

Names: it was the National Gallery of Arts. In July 2018 Culture Minister Mirela Kumbaro said it would be renamed the National Museum of Fine Arts (BalkanWeb). Shqiptarja (15 October 2025) calls Adela Demetja the new director and the first woman in the post. She told Report TV that the idea is to return it to a Museum of Fine Arts but "this is still an open discussion" (translation). Wikipedia's infobox lists Erzen Shkololli as director.
funding_verdict: National Gallery of Arts Tirana: mainly public: the Albanian state, under the Ministry of Economy, Culture and Innovation

press_items.title: Valentina Di Liscia, "Open Letter Condemns the 'Artwashing' of Albanian Prime Minister's Politics" (2020)
Hana Vranac, "Albania and Bosnia closed cultural institutions for a better future?" (2024)

name: Tirana Art Lab
overview: Non-profit centre for contemporary art in Tirana with no permanent venue. It works with local partners and keeps an office and project space at Pallati i Ri, Rruga Isa Boletini, open by appointment (Tirana Art Lab website).
Started in 2010. The website lists Adela Demetja as former founding director, 2010 to 2025, and Resina Meçani as executive director (Tirana Art Lab website).

History: 2010 to 2014 events in Tirana, Shkodra and Pogradec. 2014 to 2018 an independent space in central Tirana with an exhibition space, a residency space and a public library of contemporary art books. Since 2018 a focus on research and archiving, including Tirana Floating Archive, Tirana Floating Tours and Secondary Archive (Tirana Art Lab website).
funding_verdict: Tirana Art Lab: project-grant funded: EU, European foundations and cultural institutes, Albanian ministry and city

name: Nesr Art Foundation
overview: Independent art foundation in Luanda that runs an artist residency, a collection with an active loan programme, and educational projects, based in a creative hub with studios in Boavista (its site).
Founded in 2021 by Hiba and Wissam Nesr (its site; The Art Newspaper, 29 October 2021).
The Art Newspaper describes the founders as members of the Lebanese-Belgian family behind the Webcor Group, and Wissam Nesr as Webcor's chief executive.
funding_verdict: Nesr Art Foundation: self-funded: the founders' own money

name: Mawson's Huts
operator: Mawson's Huts Foundation and Australian Antarctic Division
overview: Wooden huts at Cape Denison, Commonwealth Bay, in the far east of the Australian Antarctic Territory, 3,000 km south of Tasmania (Australian Antarctic Division).

Built in 1912 by the Australasian Antarctic Expedition of 1911-14, led by the geologist Douglas Mawson; the main hut housed 18 men in 1912 and the seven, Mawson among them, who stayed an unplanned second year in 1913 (Mawson's Huts Foundation submission to Treasury).

Main Hut joins living quarters prefabricated in Sydney and a workshop prefabricated in Melbourne, clad in Baltic pine on an Oregon frame (Treasury submission). The site also holds Magnetograph House, the Absolute Magnetic Hut, the Transit Hut, a memorial cross and a 1931 proclamation pole (2025 heritage management plan).
funding_verdict: Mawson's Huts: government-managed site, conserved by a charity that lives mainly on replica museum and shop income plus federal grants
